boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named SDSU spaces for studying, making, gathering, recreation, and viewing art—each supported by a direct campus source.

cards.title: Settle into the Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union, first floor
cards.notes: Use the lounge’s seating for a reading break, a casual meet-up, or focused work between classes; keep the shared setting comfortable for others.
cards.short_summary: A relaxed first-floor Union space for studying and meeting up.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU identifies the Student Lounge as a first-floor Union space with seating and study areas for studying, hanging out, or taking a break.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union; check current Union operating hours before visiting.

cards.title: Make something at The Backdoor Studio
cards.subtitle: Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union, first floor
cards.notes: Plan a small creative session around the studio’s recording, music, and headshot equipment, and confirm any current use procedures before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A student creative studio for podcasts, music, and professional headshots.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU describes The Backdoor Studio as a free creative space for students with equipment for podcasts, music recording, and professional headshots.
cards.access_notes: First floor of the Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union; confirm current studio procedures and availability.

cards.title: Look for a program in Montezuma Hall
cards.subtitle: Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union, second floor
cards.notes: Check the Union and student-organization calendars, then attend a lecture, cultural showcase, or gathering that is open to the campus community.
cards.short_summary: The Union’s largest venue for campus-wide events and student gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU identifies Montezuma Hall as the Union’s largest venue and says it hosts campus-wide events, lectures, cultural showcases, and major student-organization gatherings.
cards.access_notes: Second floor of the Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union; access depends on scheduled events.

cards.title: Meet or recharge in Harvey Goodfriend Lounge
cards.subtitle: Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union, third floor
cards.notes: Choose this bright lounge for a low-key study session or conversation, and leave its tables and seating ready for the next visitors.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor lounge designed for studying, meeting up, and recharging.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU describes Harvey Goodfriend Lounge as a bright, comfortable third-floor area for studying, meeting up, or recharging.
cards.access_notes: Third floor of the Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union; check current Union operating hours.

cards.title: Check the Student Union Theatre schedule
cards.subtitle: Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union, second floor
cards.notes: Use the Union’s events listings to find a scheduled program, then arrive with time to locate the second-floor theatre before it begins.
cards.short_summary: A named second-floor theatre within the Student Union.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU’s Student Union virtual tour identifies the Student Union Theatre as a second-floor Union destination.
cards.access_notes: Second floor of the Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union; access varies with scheduled programming.

cards.title: Take a study break at Aztec Lanes
cards.subtitle: Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union, first floor
cards.notes: Arrange a bowling or billiards break with friends, and review the current facility policies, pricing, and lane availability before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor Union recreation spot with bowling and billiards.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU describes Aztec Lanes as a first-floor Union hub with bowling lanes and billiards tables for a study break or late-night hangout.
cards.access_notes: First floor of the Conrad Prebys Aztec Student Union; confirm current hours, availability, and fees before visiting.

cards.title: See an exhibition at University Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: School of Art and Design, Fourth Floor Courtyard
cards.notes: Review the exhibition calendar, then visit during academic-year gallery hours or arrange an appointment for a class tour or another visit time.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art exhibition space in the School of Art and Design.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says the University Art Gallery presents exhibitions by contemporary artists and designers and is located in the School of Art and Design’s Fourth Floor Courtyard.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Thursday, noon–4 p.m., and by appointment during the academic year; closed during winter and summer breaks.

cards.title: Walk the SDSU Mediterranean Garden
cards.subtitle: San Diego State University campus
cards.notes: Take the garden’s paths slowly, pause at the fountain and plant collections, and use the garden’s educational materials to identify its climate regions.
cards.short_summary: A planted garden representing five Mediterranean ecosystems.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU describes the Mediterranean Garden as a collection of plants from five Mediterranean ecosystems, with a fountain, patios, tables, benches, and educational value.
cards.access_notes: Use the garden’s official map and campus map for current wayfinding; respect planted areas and posted guidance.

cards.title: Spend a quiet moment in the Healing Garden
cards.subtitle: West of the Communication Building
cards.notes: Visit respectfully for a contemplative pause, using the campus interactive map for directions and giving the garden’s cultural purpose appropriate care.
cards.short_summary: A campus garden honoring Native American and Indigenous knowledge of holistic health.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says the Native and Indigenous Healing Garden honors Native American, Mesoamerican Indigenous, and California Native American communities’ knowledge of holistic health; it is west of the Communication Building.
cards.source_title: Visit | Native and Indigenous Healing Garden | SDSU
cards.access_notes: Located west of the Communication Building; use SDSU’s interactive campus map for precise location.

cards.title: Move or reset at the Aztec Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Aztec Recreation Center (ARC)
cards.notes: Choose an activity that fits your visit—court time, track, climbing, fitness studio, or quiet lounge—and verify membership access before you go.
cards.short_summary: A 134,000-square-foot recreation facility with athletic, fitness, and quiet spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says the Aztec Recreation Center includes six gymnasiums, a track, fitness studios, climbing and bouldering, and a quiet lounge.
cards.access_notes: Membership or other eligibility may be required; check the ARC’s current location, hours, and policies before visiting.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented SDSU study environments spanning quiet individual work, reservable rooms, walk-in rooms, and staffed campus spaces.

cards.entity_name: Quiet Study, Love Library Fifth Floor
cards.title: Quiet Study on Love Library’s Fifth Floor
cards.subtitle: Love Library, fifth floor
cards.notes: Head to the fifth floor when you need a library-designated quiet setting for focused reading, writing, or individual coursework.
cards.short_summary: A full-floor quiet-study option in Love Library.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU Library identifies the entire fifth floor of Love Library as Quiet Study space.
cards.access_notes: Located on the fifth floor of Love Library; consult current library access policies and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Independent Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: SDSU Library
cards.notes: Choose a study carrel, tall table, or armchair and settle into the furniture type that fits your solo work session.
cards.short_summary: Solo-work seating distributed throughout the library.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU Library says its independent-study spaces include study carrels, tall tables, and armchairs throughout the library.
cards.access_notes: These spaces are scattered throughout the library; use the library’s floor maps to select a location.

cards.title: Collaborative Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Across Love Library and the Library Addition
cards.notes: Bring a classmate or project group and use the library’s high-top tables, booths, or orb chairs for shared work.
cards.short_summary: Flexible group seating across both library buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU Library describes collaborative-study furnishings throughout both buildings, including high-top tables, booths, and orb chairs.
cards.access_notes: Available across both library buildings; select furnishings appropriate for collaborative work.

cards.title: After-Hours Study Area
cards.subtitle: Library Addition, second floor
cards.notes: Use the secure second-floor area for study space, computers, and printers when the main library has closed.
cards.short_summary: Secure library study space beyond regular hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The After-Hours Study Area provides study space, computers, and printers beyond regular library hours.
cards.source_title: After-Hours Study Area & Print Services | University Library | SDSU
cards.access_notes: On the Library Addition’s second floor; after-hours access is restricted to current SDSU students, faculty, and staff with an active SDSUid.

cards.title: After-Hours Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: After-Hours Study Area, Library Addition
cards.notes: Reserve a room for a group of at least three, then use its monitor and dry-erase board to work through shared material.
cards.short_summary: Reservable, equipped rooms for groups of three or more.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU Library offers six reservable group study rooms in the After-Hours Study Area, each with a dry-erase board and monitor.
cards.source_title: After-Hours Study Area & Print Services | University Library | SDSU
cards.access_notes: Current SDSUid is required; reserve up to two weeks ahead for up to four hours, and at least three people must be present.

cards.entity_name: Single-Use Rooms, Love Library Fourth Floor
cards.title: Love Library Single-Use Rooms
cards.subtitle: Love Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Reserve one of these compact rooms when you need privacy for a virtual interview, telehealth visit, presentation practice, or Zoom class.
cards.short_summary: Private, reservable one-person rooms for online or presentation work.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU Library’s fourth-floor Love Library single-use rooms provide a chair, table, and power for one person.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Study Room | University Library | SDSU
cards.access_notes: SDSUid, online reservation, current SDSUcard, and Circulation Desk key checkout are required; reservations are up to two hours.

cards.entity_name: Library Addition First-Floor Walk-in Study Rooms
cards.title: Library Addition First-Floor Walk-in Rooms
cards.subtitle: Research Services area, by the reference collection
cards.notes: Meet a study group near the reference collection and take an available walk-in room without making a reservation first.
cards.short_summary: Six first-come rooms beside the reference collection.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU Library lists six first-come, first-use walk-in study rooms in the Library Addition’s first-floor Research Services area.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Study Room | University Library | SDSU
cards.access_notes: Available first-come, first-use; the library gives priority to groups of three or more people.

cards.entity_name: Love Library Third-Floor Walk-in Study Rooms
cards.title: Love Library Third-Floor Walk-in Rooms
cards.subtitle: Love Library, third floor
cards.notes: Check the third-floor room cluster for an open walk-in space when your group needs a contained place to review or plan.
cards.short_summary: A listed cluster of first-come study rooms on Love Library’s third floor.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU Library lists walk-in study rooms LL-312 through LL-387 on the third floor of Love Library.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Study Room | University Library | SDSU
cards.access_notes: Available first-come, first-use; the library gives priority to groups of three or more people.

cards.entity_name: Love Library Fourth-Floor Walk-in Study Rooms
cards.title: Love Library Fourth-Floor Walk-in Rooms
cards.subtitle: Love Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Look for an unreserved room on the fourth floor when you want a walk-in option separate from the reservable single-use rooms.
cards.short_summary: First-come rooms on Love Library’s fourth floor.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU Library lists walk-in study rooms including LL-418, LL-420, LL-422, and LL-466 through LL-471 on Love Library’s fourth floor.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Study Room | University Library | SDSU
cards.access_notes: Available first-come, first-use; the library gives priority to groups of three or more people.

cards.title: Africana Studies Collection Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Love Library, third floor
cards.notes: Use the lounge-adjacent collection area for reading and laptop work, with high tables, seating clusters, outlets, and nearby workstations.
cards.short_summary: Collection-centered seating and workspace beside a third-floor lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU Library says the Africana Studies Collection on Love Library’s third floor has high tables, seating clusters, plentiful outlets, and additional computer workstations.
cards.source_title: Africana Studies Collection | University Library | SDSU
cards.access_notes: Located on Love Library’s third floor adjacent to a study lounge; follow library access policies.

cards.title: The Cowles Mountain S

cards.notes: Learn the history through SDSU’s account and seek only sanctioned campus displays; do not climb, paint, or alter Cowles Mountain.
